```text
import type { ExcalidrawElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import { getDefaultAppState } from "./appState";

import type { AppState } from "./types";

export type PageSettings = Pick<
  AppState,
  | "viewBackgroundColor"
  | "scrollX"
  | "scrollY"
  | "zoom"
  | "gridSize"
  | "gridStep"
  | "gridScale"
  | "gridSnapLinked"
  | "gridSnapScale"
  | "gridColor"
  | "gridOpacity"
  | "gridLayer"
  | "gridModeEnabled"
  | "gridSnapEnabled"
  | "frameRendering"
>;

export type DrawingPage = Readonly<{
  id: string;
  elements: readonly ExcalidrawElement[];
  settings: PageSettings;
}>;

export const getPageSettings = (appState: PageSettings): PageSettings => ({
  viewBackgroundColor: appState.viewBackgroundColor,
  scrollX: appState.scrollX,
  scrollY: appState.scrollY,
  zoom: appState.zoom,
  gridSize: appState.gridSize,
  gridStep: appState.gridStep,
  gridScale: appState.gridScale,
  gridSnapLinked: appState.gridSnapLinked,
  gridSnapScale: appState.gridSnapScale,
  gridColor: appState.gridColor,
  gridOpacity: appState.gridOpacity,
  gridLayer: appState.gridLayer,
  gridModeEnabled: appState.gridModeEnabled,
  gridSnapEnabled: appState.gridSnapEnabled,
  frameRendering: appState.frameRendering,
});

export const createPage = (id: string): DrawingPage => ({
  id,
  elements: [],
  settings: getPageSettings(getDefaultAppState()),
});
import React, { useEffect, useState } from "react";

import { isNonDeletedElement } from "@excalidraw/element";

import { exportToCanvas } from "../scene/export";

import { getDefaultAppState } from "../appState";
import { t } from "../i18n";

import "./Pages.scss";

import type { BinaryFiles, UIAppState } from "../types";
import type { DrawingPage } from "../pages";

const PAGE_PREVIEW_WIDTH = 144;
const PAGE_PREVIEW_HEIGHT = 96;

const PageIcon = () => (
  <svg
    aria-hidden="true"
    width="20"
    height="20"
    viewBox="0 0 24 24"
    fill="none"
    stroke="currentColor"
    strokeWidth="1.5"
    strokeLinecap="round"
    strokeLinejoin="round"
  >
    <rect x="4" y="3" width="16" height="18" rx="2" />
    <path d="M8 8h8M8 12h8M8 16h5" />
  </svg>
);

const PagePreview = React.memo(
  ({
    page,
    files,
    appState,
  }: {
    page: DrawingPage;
    files: BinaryFiles;
    appState: UIAppState;
  }) => {
    const [previewUrl, setPreviewUrl] = useState<string | null>(null);

    useEffect(() => {
      let active = true;
      const elements = page.elements.filter(isNonDeletedElement);

      if (!elements.length) {
        setPreviewUrl(null);
        return;
      }

      const timeout = window.setTimeout(() => {
        const defaultAppState = getDefaultAppState();
        const previewAppState = {
          ...defaultAppState,
          ...appState,
          ...page.settings,
          width: appState.width,
          height: appState.height,
          offsetTop: 0,
          offsetLeft: 0,
          scrollX: 0,
          scrollY: 0,
          zoom: defaultAppState.zoom,
        };

        void exportToCanvas(
          elements,
          previewAppState,
          files,
          {
            exportBackground: true,
            exportPadding: 8,
            viewBackgroundColor: page.settings.viewBackgroundColor,
          },
          (width, height) => {
            const scale = Math.min(
              PAGE_PREVIEW_WIDTH / Math.max(width, 1),
              PAGE_PREVIEW_HEIGHT / Math.max(height, 1),
              1,
            );
            const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
            canvas.width = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(width * scale));
            canvas.height = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(height * scale));
            return { canvas, scale };
          },
        )
          .then((canvas) => {
            if (active) {
              setPreviewUrl(canvas.toDataURL());
            }
          })
          .catch((error: unknown) => {
            console.error("Failed to render page preview", error);
          });
      }, 250);

      return () => {
        active = false;
        window.clearTimeout(timeout);
      };
    }, [appState, files, page]);

    return previewUrl ? (
      <img className="page-navigation__preview" src={previewUrl} alt="" />
    ) : (
      <span
        className="page-navigation__preview page-navigation__preview--empty"
        aria-hidden="true"
      />
    );
  },
  (prevProps, nextProps) =>
    prevProps.page === nextProps.page &&
    prevProps.files === nextProps.files &&
    prevProps.appState.exportWithDarkMode ===
      nextProps.appState.exportWithDarkMode &&
    prevProps.appState.theme === nextProps.appState.theme,
);

export const Pages = ({
  pages,
  activePageId,
  appState,
  files,
  onSelectPage,
  onCreatePage,
}: {
  pages: readonly DrawingPage[];
  activePageId: string;
  appState: UIAppState;
  files: BinaryFiles;
  onSelectPage: (pageId: string) => void;
  onCreatePage: () => void;
}) => (
  <div className="page-navigation" role="region" aria-label={t("labels.pages")}>
    <div className="page-navigation__list">
      {pages.map((page, index) => (
        <button
          type="button"
          key={page.id}
          className="page-navigation__item"
          aria-label={`${t("labels.page")} ${index + 1}`}
          aria-pressed={page.id === activePageId}
          onClick={() => onSelectPage(page.id)}
        >
          <PagePreview page={page} files={files} appState={appState} />
          <span className="page-navigation__item-title">
            {t("labels.page")} {index + 1}
          </span>
        </button>
      ))}
    </div>
    <button
      type="button"
      className="page-navigation__add"
      onClick={onCreatePage}
      disabled={appState.viewModeEnabled}
    >
      <span aria-hidden="true">+</span>
      {t("buttons.addPage")}
    </button>
  </div>
);

export { PageIcon };

+  private saveActivePage = () => {
+    const activePage = this.pages.find((page) => page.id === this.activePageId);
+    if (!activePage) {
+      throw new Error(`Active page ${this.activePageId} does not exist`);
+    }
+
+    this.pages = this.pages.map((page) =>
+      page.id === this.activePageId
+        ? {
+            ...page,
+            elements: this.scene.getElementsIncludingDeleted(),
+            settings: getPageSettings(this.state),
+          }
+        : page,
+    );
+  };
+
+  private getPagesForUI = (): readonly DrawingPage[] => {
+    const elements = this.scene.getElementsIncludingDeleted();
+    const settings = getPageSettings(this.state);
+    return this.pages.map((page) =>
+      page.id === this.activePageId ? { ...page, elements, settings } : page,
+    );
+  };
+
+  private selectPage = (pageId: string) => {
+    const page = this.pages.find((candidate) => candidate.id === pageId);
+    if (!page) {
+      throw new Error(`Cannot select unknown page ${pageId}`);
+    }
+    if (pageId === this.activePageId) {
+      return;
+    }
+
+    this.saveActivePage();
+    this.activePageId = pageId;
+    this.history.clear();
+    this.updateScene({
+      elements: page.elements,
+      appState: getPageActivationAppState(page.settings),
+      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
+    });
+  };
+
+  private createPage = () => {
+    const page = createPage(nanoid());
+    this.saveActivePage();
+    this.pages = [...this.pages, page];
+    this.activePageId = page.id;
+    this.history.clear();
+    this.updateScene({
+      elements: page.elements,
+      appState: getPageActivationAppState(page.settings),
+      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
+    });
+  };
```

Pages aren't part of upstream Excalidraw. Your team added them in PR #178 (commits `43e7cdaa` and `240ab7e2`), and they're stored only in memory inside the editor.

## How they're configured

**Data model: `packages/excalidraw/pages.ts`**
- `DrawingPage` holds an `id`, that page's `elements`, and a `settings` object.
- `PageSettings` is the per-page slice of `AppState`: background color, scroll position, zoom, all the grid settings, and `frameRendering`. Everything else in `AppState` (tool, styles, theme, etc.) is shared across pages.
- `createPage(id)` returns a page with no elements and the default settings from `getDefaultAppState()`.
- `getPageSettings(appState)` copies the per-page fields out of the current state.

**State: `packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx`**
- `App` has two private fields: `this.pages: DrawingPage[]` and `this.activePageId`. The constructor starts with one page.
- The active page's real data lives in the scene (`this.scene` / `this.state`). Its entry in `this.pages` is out of date until the page is saved.
- `saveActivePage()` writes the current scene elements and settings back into `this.pages`.
- `selectPage(id)` saves the current page, switches `activePageId`, clears undo history, and loads the target page with `updateScene(..., CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER)`. It also resets selection and editing state through `getPageActivationAppState`.
- `createPage()` works the same way, but first adds a new empty page to the list.
- `getPagesForUI()` builds the list the UI shows, swapping in the live scene for the active page so its preview stays current.

**UI**
- `components/Pages.tsx`: the `Pages` panel. It lists each page with a thumbnail (made by `exportToCanvas`, delayed 250ms) and has an "Add page" button, which is disabled in view mode.
- `components/LayerUI.tsx`: adds a "pages" tab (`PAGES_SIDEBAR_TAB`) to the default sidebar and puts a Pages button in the top-right UI.
- `components/DefaultSidebar.tsx` and `context/tunnels.ts`: add a new `DefaultSidebar.TabContents` slot (backed by `DefaultSidebarTabContentsTunnel`), so built-in tabs can be added next to tabs a host app provides.
- `components/MobileMenu.tsx`: the same Pages button for mobile.
- `locales/en.json`: the strings `labels.pages`, `labels.page` and `buttons.addPage`.

## How to make a page

**As a user:** click the Pages icon in the top-right, or open the sidebar's pages tab, then click **+ Add page**. Click any thumbnail to switch to that page.

**In code:** there's no public API yet. `createPage` and `selectPage` are private methods on `App`, so you can't call them from `excalidrawAPI` or from `excalidraw-app`. Inside `App` you'd call `this.createPage()`. To expose it, add those methods to the imperative API that `App` builds for `excalidrawAPI`. `tests/pages.test.tsx` shows the current flow by clicking the "Pages" and "Add page" buttons.

## Current limitations
- **Not saved anywhere:** pages aren't written to localStorage, `.excalidraw` export, or `restore`. Only the active page's elements reach `onChange`, so reloading the app loses every other page.
- **Not collaborative:** collab only syncs the active scene.
- **Undo history is cleared** whenever you switch or create a page.
- **No delete, rename or reorder.** Pages are just labeled "Page N" by their position.

Your branch (`feat/issue-159-page-clearing`) presumably builds on `saveActivePage` and `selectPage`. For example, clearing a page could mean resetting the active scene, or replacing that page's `elements` in `this.pages` when it isn't the active one.

Closing clearing mode: The clearing options should only be visible when in clearing mode. Clearing mode should remain open until the user selects the exit option, which closes clearing mode.

I'd split this into four parts: a per-editor state field for clearing mode, a few page-clearing methods on `App`, a clearing mode in the Pages sidebar, and a second choice in the existing Clear canvas dialog.

**Key point first:** don't store clearing mode, or its confirm dialog, in an editor jotai atom. `packages/excalidraw/editor-jotai.ts` creates one module-level `editorJotaiStore`, and every `<Excalidraw>` on the page shares it. If clearing mode lived there, entering it in one drawing would enter it in the other, which fails your "page groups" criterion.

The existing Clear canvas dialog has the same problem: `activeConfirmDialogAtom` is global, so pressing Ctrl+Delete in one editor opens the dialog in every editor. State on `AppState`, or a component's own `useState`, belongs to one editor, so that's where clearing mode should go.

## 1. State: a new `AppState` field

```ts
// types.ts → AppState
/** null = not in clearing mode; otherwise the page ids selected for clearing */
pageClearingSelection: string[] | null;
```

- **`appState.ts`:** set the default to `null`. Add `pageClearingSelection: { browser: false, export: false, server: false }` to `APP_STATE_STORAGE_CONF` so it's never saved or exported.
- **Why `AppState` and not a private field next to `this.pages`:**
  - Each editor gets its own copy.
  - Changing it re-renders the UI.
  - `DefaultSidebar` can read it through `useUIAppState()` (see section 3).
  - If the sidebar closes, the mode stays on, so it only ends when the user clicks Exit.
- **Page switching:** `getPageActivationAppState` only spreads page settings and resets selection, so switching pages won't touch this field. Don't add it there.
- **Clear canvas side effect:** `actionClearCanvas` resets the app state to `getDefaultAppState()`, which would set this field back to `null` and exit clearing mode. Either keep `pageClearingSelection: appState.pageClearingSelection` in its returned state, or accept that behavior on purpose.

## 2. Page-clearing methods on `App.tsx`

Put these next to `selectPage` and `createPage`:

```ts
public getPageIds = () => this.pages.map((p) => p.id);
public getActivePageId = () => this.activePageId;

private enterPageClearingMode = () =>
  this.setState({ pageClearingSelection: [] });

private exitPageClearingMode = () =>
  this.setState({ pageClearingSelection: null });

private togglePageForClearing = (pageId: string) =>
  this.setState((s) => {
    const sel = s.pageClearingSelection ?? [];
    return {
      pageClearingSelection: sel.includes(pageId)
        ? sel.filter((id) => id !== pageId)
        : [...sel, pageId],
    };
  });

private setAllPagesForClearing = (selected: boolean) =>
  this.setState({ pageClearingSelection: selected ? this.getPageIds() : [] });

public clearPages = (pageIds: readonly string[]) => {
  const ids = new Set(pageIds);
  // Inactive pages: their data lives only in this.pages
  this.pages = this.pages.map((page) =>
    ids.has(page.id) && page.id !== this.activePageId
      ? { ...page, elements: [] }
      : page,
  );
  // Active page: its data lives in the scene
  if (ids.has(this.activePageId)) {
    this.updateScene({
      elements: this.scene
        .getElementsIncludingDeleted()
        .map((el) => newElementWith(el, { isDeleted: true })),
      appState: { selectedElementIds: {}, selectedGroupIds: {}, editingGroupId: null },
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY,
    });
  } else {
    this.forceUpdate(); // refresh the page previews
  }
};
```

Notes:
- **Inactive pages are set to `[]`.** Pages aren't synced over collab, so there's no need to keep deleted elements around as tombstones.
- **Page settings stay the same.** The criteria say to clear elements, so background, scroll and grid settings are left alone.
- **Image files are left alone.** `this.files` is shared across all pages, so deleting binary files could break images on pages that weren't cleared.
- **Undo is inconsistent.** Clearing the active page can be undone, but cleared inactive pages can't. If the team wants it consistent, use `CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER` plus `this.history.clear()` for the active page too.

Pass `pageClearingSelection`, `activePageId` and the new callbacks through `LayerUI` to `<Pages>`, the same way `onPageSelect` and `onPageCreate` are passed now.

## 3. UI in `Pages.tsx`, `Pages.scss` and `DefaultSidebar.tsx`

**Normal mode** (`pageClearingSelection === null`):
- The current list stays as it is.
- Add an **"Enter clearing mode"** button next to "Add page". Disable it in view mode.

**Clearing mode** (the augmented navigation menu, in the same sidebar tab):
- **Each page item** becomes a checkbox-style button: `role="checkbox"` with `aria-checked`, and clicking it calls `onToggleClear(page.id)` instead of switching pages.
  - Show selection with a check mark and an accent border.
  - Show the current page separately with a "Current" badge and `aria-current="page"`, so a page can look both current and selected.
- **Footer buttons:**
  - **Select all / Deselect all**, based on whether every page is selected.
  - **Clear**, disabled when nothing is selected.
  - **Exit clearing mode**.
- **Confirmation:** keep it inside `<Pages>` with local state (`const [confirming, setConfirming] = useState(false)`) and render `<ConfirmDialog onConfirm={() => { onClearPages(selection); setConfirming(false); }} …>`. Local state belongs to one editor, so it can't leak to another drawing.
  - For example: "Clear N selected page(s)? This removes all elements on those pages."
  - After a confirmed clear, I'd stay in clearing mode and reset the selection to `[]`, because the criteria say the mode only closes on Exit.
- **"Open a menu to the side":** `DefaultSidebar.tsx` already forces the sidebar to dock for search (`isForceDocked = appState.openSidebar?.tab === CANVAS_SEARCH_TAB`). Extend that rule to `|| appState.pageClearingSelection !== null`. A docked sidebar shrinks the canvas instead of covering it and doesn't close on outside clicks, so the user can see the current page the whole time.
- **Strings:** add `buttons.enterClearingMode`, `exitClearingMode`, `clearPages`, `selectAllPages`, `deselectAllPages`, `labels.currentPage`, plus a `clearPagesDialog.title` and body to `locales/en.json`.

## 4. Changing the existing Clear canvas option

Today the main menu, Ctrl+Delete and the command palette all set `activeConfirmDialogAtom = "clearCanvas"`. `ActiveConfirmDialog.tsx` then runs `actionClearCanvas`.

**Pass a scope through the action's `value` argument.** `executeAction(action, source, value)` passes `value` into `perform` as its third argument, which `actionClearCanvas` currently ignores as `_`:

```ts
// actionCanvas.tsx
perform: (elements, appState, value: { scope?: "canvas" | "all" } | null, app) => {
  if (value?.scope === "all") {
    app.clearPages(app.getPageIds()); // inactive pages; active one is cleared below
  }
  app.imageCache.clear();
  return { /* existing body unchanged */ };
},
```

- Add `clearPages`, `getPageIds` and `getActivePageId` to the `AppClassProperties` type in `types.ts` (around line 969) so `app.` can see them.
- **Order matters:** `clearPages` has to run inside `perform`, before the action's returned elements are applied, so the active page ends up cleared by the existing return value.

**The dialog** (`ActiveConfirmDialog.tsx`):
- Use `useApp()`, which App.tsx exports at line 649.
- When `app.getPageIds().length > 1`, show two buttons:
  - **"Clear this canvas only"** → `executeAction(actionClearCanvas, "ui", { scope: "canvas" })`
  - **"Clear canvas and all pages"** → `executeAction(actionClearCanvas, "ui", { scope: "all" })`
- `ConfirmDialog` only has one confirm button, so either add an optional `secondaryAction` prop or build the dialog from `Dialog` and `DialogActionButton`.
- With only one page, keep today's single-button dialog.
- **Optional:** move this dialog's state off the global atom (for example into `AppState.openDialog`) to fix the cross-editor problem described at the top. That's a small, separate change.

## 5. Tests (extend `tests/pages.test.tsx`)

- Enter clearing mode, check that the current page is marked, select page 2, click Clear, confirm, and check that only page 2 is empty. Then do the same with Select all.
- Cancel at the confirm dialog and check that nothing changed.
- Click Exit and check that the clearing controls are gone. Close and reopen the sidebar and check that clearing mode is still on.
- Render two `<Excalidraw>`s, scope queries with `within(container)`, enter clearing mode in one, and check that the other is unaffected. `window.h` only points at the last editor mounted, so assert through the DOM.
- Clear canvas with 2+ pages, once for each scope.

```bash
    this.activePageId = page.id;
    this.history.clear();
    this.updateScene({
      elements: page.elements,
      appState: getPageActivationAppState(page.settings),
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
    });
  };

  public getPageIds = (): string[] => this.pages.map((page) => page.id);

  public getActivePageId = (): string => this.activePageId;

  /**
   * Removes all elements from the given pages, keeping the (now empty) pages
   * and their settings. Clearing the active page is undoable; clearing other
   * pages is not, since history only tracks the active page.
   */
  public clearPages = (pageIds: readonly string[]) => {
    const ids = new Set(pageIds);

    this.pages = this.pages.map((page) =>
      ids.has(page.id) && page.id !== this.activePageId
        ? { ...page, elements: [] }
        : page,
    );

    if (ids.has(this.activePageId)) {
      this.updateScene({
        elements: this.scene
          .getElementsIncludingDeleted()
          .map((element) =>
            element.isDeleted
              ? element
              : newElementWith(element, { isDeleted: true }),
          ),
        appState: {
          selectedElementIds: {},
          selectedGroupIds: {},
          editingGroupId: null,
        },
        captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY,
      });
    } else {
      // inactive pages live outside React state; re-render their previews
      this.forceUpdate();
    }
  };

  private enterPageClearingMode = () => {
    this.setState({ pageClearingSelection: [] });
  };

  private exitPageClearingMode = () => {
    this.setState({ pageClearingSelection: null });
  };

  private togglePageForClearing = (pageId: string) => {
    this.setState((state) => {
      if (!state.pageClearingSelection) {
        return null;
      }
      const selection = state.pageClearingSelection;
      return {
        pageClearingSelection: selection.includes(pageId)
          ? selection.filter((id) => id !== pageId)
          : [...selection, pageId],
      };
    });
  };

  private setAllPagesForClearing = (selected: boolean) => {
    this.setState({
      pageClearingSelection: selected ? this.getPageIds() : [],
    });
  };

  private clearSelectedPages = () => {
    const selection = this.state.pageClearingSelection;
    if (!selection?.length) {
      return;
    }
    this.clearPages(selection);
    // stay in clearing mode until the user explicitly exits it
    this.setState({ pageClearingSelection: [] });
  };
''')
```

```bash
import { flushSync } from "react-dom";

import { useSetAtom } from "../editor-jotai";
import { t } from "../i18n";

import { Dialog } from "./Dialog";
import DialogActionButton from "./DialogActionButton";
import { isLibraryMenuOpenAtom } from "./LibraryMenu";
import { useExcalidrawContainer, useExcalidrawSetAppState } from "./App";

import "./ConfirmDialog.scss";

import type { DialogProps } from "./Dialog";

interface Props extends Omit<DialogProps, "onCloseRequest"> {
  onConfirm: () => void;
  onCancel: () => void;
  confirmText?: string;
  cancelText?: string;
  /** optional second confirm action, rendered between cancel and confirm */
  onSecondaryConfirm?: () => void;
  secondaryConfirmText?: string;
}
const ConfirmDialog = (props: Props) => {
  const {
    onConfirm,
    onCancel,
    onSecondaryConfirm,
    children,
    confirmText = t("buttons.confirm"),
    cancelText = t("buttons.cancel"),
    secondaryConfirmText = t("buttons.confirm"),
    className = "",
    ...rest
  } = props;
  const setAppState = useExcalidrawSetAppState();
  const setIsLibraryMenuOpen = useSetAtom(isLibraryMenuOpenAtom);
  const { container } = useExcalidrawContainer();

  const runAndRefocus = (callback: () => void) => {
    setAppState({ openMenu: null });
    setIsLibraryMenuOpen(false);
    // flush any pending updates synchronously,
    // otherwise it could lead to crash in some chromium versions (131.0.6778.86),
    // when `.focus` is invoked with container in some intermediate state
    // (container seems mounted in DOM, but focus still causes a crash)
    flushSync(() => {
      callback();
    });

    container?.focus();
  };

  return (
    <Dialog
      onCloseRequest={onCancel}
      size="small"
      {...rest}
      className={`confirm-dialog ${className}`}
    >
      {children}
      <div className="confirm-dialog-buttons">
        <DialogActionButton
          label={cancelText}
          onClick={() => runAndRefocus(onCancel)}
        />
        {onSecondaryConfirm && (
          <DialogActionButton
            label={secondaryConfirmText}
            onClick={() => runAndRefocus(onSecondaryConfirm)}
            actionType="danger"
          />
        )}
        <DialogActionButton
          label={confirmText}
          onClick={() => runAndRefocus(onConfirm)}
          actionType="danger"
        />
      </div>
    </Dialog>
  );
};
export default ConfirmDialog;
EOF
```

```bash
import { actionClearCanvas } from "../actions";
import { atom, useAtom } from "../editor-jotai";
import { t } from "../i18n";

import { useApp, useExcalidrawActionManager } from "./App";
import ConfirmDialog from "./ConfirmDialog";

export const activeConfirmDialogAtom = atom<"clearCanvas" | null>(null);

export const ActiveConfirmDialog = () => {
  const [activeConfirmDialog, setActiveConfirmDialog] = useAtom(
    activeConfirmDialogAtom,
  );
  const actionManager = useExcalidrawActionManager();
  const app = useApp();

  if (!activeConfirmDialog) {
    return null;
  }

  if (activeConfirmDialog === "clearCanvas") {
    // the canvas is the active page; other pages are its sub-canvases
    const hasOtherPages = app.getPageIds().length > 1;

    if (hasOtherPages) {
      return (
        <ConfirmDialog
          onSecondaryConfirm={() => {
            actionManager.executeAction(actionClearCanvas, "ui", {
              scope: "canvas",
            });
            setActiveConfirmDialog(null);
          }}
          secondaryConfirmText={t("buttons.clearCanvasOnly")}
          onConfirm={() => {
            actionManager.executeAction(actionClearCanvas, "ui", {

            });
            setActiveConfirmDialog(null);
          }}
          confirmText={t("buttons.clearCanvasAndPages")}
          onCancel={() => setActiveConfirmDialog(null)}
          title={t("clearCanvasDialog.title")}
        >
          <p className="clear-canvas__content">
            {t("clearCanvasDialog.withPages")}
          </p>
        </ConfirmDialog>
      );
    }

    return (
      <ConfirmDialog
        onConfirm={() => {
          actionManager.executeAction(actionClearCanvas);
          setActiveConfirmDialog(null);
        }}
        onCancel={() => setActiveConfirmDialog(null)}
        title={t("clearCanvasDialog.title")}
      >
        <p className="clear-canvas__content"> {t("alerts.clearReset")}</p>
      </ConfirmDialog>
    );
  }

  return null;
};
```

```text
import type { Action } from "./types";

export let actions: readonly Action[] = [];

export const register = <
  TData extends any,
  T extends Action<TData> = Action<TData>,
>(
  action: T,
) => {
  actions = actions.concat(action);
  return action as T & {
    keyTest?: unknown extends T["keyTest"] ? never : T["keyTest"];
  };
};
```

```text
    initLocalStorage(options.localStorageData);
```

```typescript
      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Enter clearing mode" }));

      expect(window.h.state.pageClearingSelection).toEqual([]);
      expect(getByRole("button", { name: "Clear" })).toBeTruthy();
      expect(getByRole("button", { name: "Select all pages" })).toBeTruthy();
      expect(
        queryByRole("button", { name: "Enter clearing mode" }),
      ).toBeNull();
      expect(queryByRole("button", { name: "Add page" })).toBeNull();
      // the page the user is on is indicated
      expect(
        getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Page 3" }).getAttribute("aria-current"),
      ).toBe("page");
      expect(
        getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Page 1" }).getAttribute("aria-current"),
      ).toBeNull();
      // nothing selected yet → nothing to clear
      expect(
        (getByRole("button", { name: "Clear" }) as HTMLButtonElement).disabled,
      ).toBe(true);

      // closing the sidebar does not exit clearing mode
      API.setAppState({ openSidebar: null });
      expect(window.h.state.pageClearingSelection).toEqual([]);
      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Pages" }));
      expect(getByRole("button", { name: "Exit clearing mode" })).toBeTruthy();

      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Exit clearing mode" }));

      expect(window.h.state.pageClearingSelection).toBeNull();
      expect(queryByRole("button", { name: "Clear" })).toBeNull();
      expect(queryByRole("checkbox", { name: "Page 1" })).toBeNull();
      expect(
        getByRole("button", { name: "Enter clearing mode" }),
      ).toBeTruthy();
    });

    it("docks the pages sidebar while in clearing mode", async () => {
      const { getByRole, container } = await renderWithThreePages();
      API.setAppState({ defaultSidebarDockedPreference: false });

      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Enter clearing mode" }));

      await waitFor(() => {
        expect(
          container.querySelector(".default-sidebar.sidebar--docked"),
        ).not.toBeNull();
      });
    });

    it("selects pages, confirms, and clears only the selected pages", async () => {
      const { getByRole } = await renderWithThreePages();

      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Enter clearing mode" }));
      // selecting a page does not navigate away from the current page
      fireEvent.click(getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Page 1" }));
      expect(liveIds()).toEqual(["page-three"]);
      expect(
        getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Page 1" }).getAttribute("aria-checked"),
      ).toBe("true");
      expect(
        getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Page 2" }).getAttribute("aria-checked"),
      ).toBe("false");

      // toggling a page twice leaves it unselected
      fireEvent.click(getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Page 2" }));
      fireEvent.click(getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Page 2" }));
      expect(window.h.state.pageClearingSelection).toHaveLength(1);

      // cancelling the confirmation clears nothing
      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Clear" }));
      fireEvent.click(
        getConfirmDialog().getByRole("button", { name: "Cancel" }),
      );
      expect(document.querySelector(".confirm-dialog")).toBeNull();
      expect(window.h.state.pageClearingSelection).toHaveLength(1);

      // confirming clears the selected page
      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Clear" }));
      fireEvent.click(getConfirmDialog().getByRole("button", { name: "Clear" }));

      // still in clearing mode, with the selection reset
      expect(window.h.state.pageClearingSelection).toEqual([]);
      expect(liveIds()).toEqual(["page-three"]);

      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Exit clearing mode" }));
      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Page 1" }));
      await waitFor(() => expect(liveIds()).toEqual([]));
      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Page 2" }));
      await waitFor(() => expect(liveIds()).toEqual(["page-two"]));
      // cleared pages are kept
      expect(getByRole("button", { name: "Page 3" })).toBeTruthy();
    });

    it("selects all pages and clears them, including the current one", async () => {
      const { getByRole } = await renderWithThreePages();

      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Enter clearing mode" }));
      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Select all pages" }));
      for (const name of ["Page 1", "Page 2", "Page 3"]) {
        expect(
          getByRole("checkbox", { name }).getAttribute("aria-checked"),
        ).toBe("true");
      }

      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Deselect all pages" }));
      expect(window.h.state.pageClearingSelection).toEqual([]);
      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Select all pages" }));

      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Clear" }));
      fireEvent.click(getConfirmDialog().getByRole("button", { name: "Clear" }));

      expect(liveIds()).toEqual([]);
      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Exit clearing mode" }));
      for (const name of ["Page 1", "Page 2"]) {
        fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name }));
        await waitFor(() => expect(liveIds()).toEqual([]));
      }
    });

    it("is scoped to a single drawing", async () => {
      const { container } = await render(
        <>
          <div data-testid="first">
            <Excalidraw initialData={{ elements: [] }} />
          </div>
          <div data-testid="second">
            <Excalidraw initialData={{ elements: [] }} />
          </div>
        </>,
      );
      const first = within(
        container.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-testid="first"]')!,
      );
      const second = within(
        container.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-testid="second"]')!,
      );

      fireEvent.click(first.getByRole("button", { name: "Pages" }));
      fireEvent.click(second.getByRole("button", { name: "Pages" }));

      // entering in one drawing does not enter in the other
      fireEvent.click(
        first.getByRole("button", { name: "Enter clearing mode" }),
      );
      expect(
        first.getByRole("button", { name: "Exit clearing mode" }),
      ).toBeTruthy();
      expect(
        second.queryByRole("button", { name: "Exit clearing mode" }),
      ).toBeNull();

      // exiting in one drawing does not exit in the other
      fireEvent.click(
        second.getByRole("button", { name: "Enter clearing mode" }),
      );
      fireEvent.click(
        first.getByRole("button", { name: "Exit clearing mode" }),
      );
      expect(
        first.queryByRole("button", { name: "Exit clearing mode" }),
      ).toBeNull();
      expect(
        second.getByRole("button", { name: "Exit clearing mode" }),
      ).toBeTruthy();
    });
  });

  describe("clear canvas", () => {
    const openClearCanvasDialog = () => {
      Keyboard.withModifierKeys({ ctrl: true }, () => {
        Keyboard.keyDown(KEYS.DELETE);
      });
      return getConfirmDialog();
    };

    it("can clear only the current page", async () => {
      const { getByRole } = await renderWithPages(["page-one", "page-two"]);

      fireEvent.click(
        openClearCanvasDialog().getByRole("button", {
          name: "Clear this canvas only",
        }),
      );

      await waitFor(() => expect(liveIds()).toEqual([]));
      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Pages" }));
      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Page 1" }));
      await waitFor(() => expect(liveIds()).toEqual(["page-one"]));
    });

    it("can clear the current page and all other pages", async () => {
      const { getByRole } = await renderWithPages(["page-one", "page-two"]);

      fireEvent.click(
        openClearCanvasDialog().getByRole("button", {
          name: "Clear canvas and all pages",
        }),
      );

      await waitFor(() => expect(liveIds()).toEqual([]));
      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Pages" }));
      // pages are kept, but empty
      expect(getByRole("button", { name: "Page 2" })).toBeTruthy();
      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Page 1" }));
      await waitFor(() => expect(window.h.elements).toHaveLength(0));
    });

    it("keeps the single confirm option when there is only one page", async () => {
      await render(
        <Excalidraw
          initialData={{
            elements: [API.createElement({ type: "rectangle" })],
          }}
          handleKeyboardGlobally
        />,
      );

      const dialog = openClearCanvasDialog();
      expect(
        dialog.queryByRole("button", { name: "Clear this canvas only" }),
      ).toBeNull();
      expect(dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Confirm" })).toBeTruthy();
    });
  });
});
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-19 04:11:24Z)**_

Page clearing is implemented on `feat/issue-159-page-clearing`. The 8 new tests and the existing pages test all pass, along with typecheck and lint. I haven't committed anything.

The full suite (`yarn test:update`) had 2 failures, neither from this change:
- **`pathPlaybackHold.test.tsx`:** your untracked work-in-progress test. It fails the same way with my changes stashed.
- **`MermaidToExcalidraw.test.tsx`:** flaky. It passed on a rerun.

## How it meets the acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Implementation |
|---|---|
| **Clearing mode** | The Pages sidebar now has an **Enter clearing mode** button under **+ Add page**. In clearing mode the sidebar stays docked beside the canvas, so the current page stays visible. Each page has a checkbox, and the page you're on has a **Current** badge. |
| **Clear selection** | Clicking a page selects or deselects it instead of switching to it. A **Select all pages / Deselect all pages** button toggles everything. Selected pages get a check mark and a red border. |
| **Clearing confirmation** | **Clear** is disabled until at least one page is selected. It opens a confirmation dialog; cancelling changes nothing, and confirming empties the selected pages. Cleared pages keep their settings. |
| **Closing clearing mode** | Clearing controls only appear in clearing mode, and **Add page** is hidden while it's on. Mode stays on after a clear (the selection resets) and even if the sidebar is closed. It ends only on **Exit clearing mode**. |
| **Across page groups** | The state is a new per-editor `AppState.pageClearingSelection` field (`null` means off), and the confirmation uses local component state. Two drawings on the same page don't affect each other, and a test checks this. |
| **Clear canvas option** | With more than one page, the existing dialog (main menu, Ctrl+Delete, command palette) offers **Clear this canvas only** or **Clear canvas and all pages**. Clearing all keeps the pages, just empty. With one page the dialog works as before. |

## What changed
- **`App.tsx`:** new public `getPageIds`, `getActivePageId` and `clearPages`, plus private methods for entering, exiting, selecting and clearing in clearing mode.
- **`Pages.tsx` / `Pages.scss`:** the clearing-mode UI and its confirmation dialog.
- **`actionCanvas.tsx`:** `actionClearCanvas` takes `{ scope: "canvas" | "allPages" }`. Clear canvas also no longer exits clearing mode.
- **`ActiveConfirmDialog.tsx`:** the two-option dialog.
- **`ConfirmDialog.tsx`:** an optional second confirm button.
- **`DefaultSidebar.tsx`:** docks the sidebar while clearing mode is on.
- **`types.ts`, `appState.ts`, `LayerUI.tsx`, `en.json`:** the new state field (never saved or exported), the props passed through, and the new strings.
- **Tests:** 8 new cases in `pages.test.tsx`. The snapshot changes are only `"pageClearingSelection": null`. I restored the Mermaid and `scene/export` snapshots, which `test:update` had changed for reasons unrelated to this work.

## Things to know
- **Undo:** clearing the page you're on can be undone, but clearing other pages can't, because undo history only covers the active page.
- **Existing shared dialog:** the existing Clear canvas dialog still uses a state store shared by all editors on the page, so with two drawings, Ctrl+Delete in one opens the dialog in both. That was true before this change and isn't one of your criteria.
- **Leftover snapshots:** `scene/export.test.ts.snap` contains snapshots no test uses anymore, added by the earlier pages commit. I left them alone.

Do you want me to commit this and open a PR against `master`?

```javascript
(async () => {
  const browser = await puppeteer.launch({
    executablePath: "C:/Program Files (x86)/Microsoft/Edge/Application/msedge.exe",
    headless: true,

  });
  const page = await browser.newPage();
  page.on("pageerror", (e) => console.log("pageerror", e.message));
  await page.goto("http://localhost:3123", { waitUntil: "networkidle2", timeout: 120000 });

  // dismiss welcome screen etc.

  const clickByText = (text) =>

      const b = [...document.querySelectorAll(".page-navigation button")].find(
        (el) => el.textContent.trim().endsWith(text),
      );
      b.click();
    }, text);

  for (let i = 0; i < 9; i++) {

    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 150));
  }

  const measure = () =>
    page.evaluate(() => {
      const list = document.querySelector(".page-navigation__list");
      const sidebar = document.querySelector(".default-sidebar");
      const actions = document.querySelector(".page-navigation__actions");
      const sr = sidebar.getBoundingClientRect();
      const ar = actions.getBoundingClientRect();
      return {
        items: list.children.length,
        listClient: list.clientHeight,
        listScroll: list.scrollHeight,
        overflowY: getComputedStyle(list).overflowY,
        sidebarBottom: Math.round(sr.bottom),
        actionsBottom: Math.round(ar.bottom),
        actionsVisible: ar.bottom <= sr.bottom + 1,
      };
    });

  console.log("after adding pages:", await measure());
  await page.screenshot({ path: `${OUT}/pages-top.png` });

  await page.evaluate(() => {
    const list = document.querySelector(".page-navigation__list");
    list.scrollTop = list.scrollHeight;
  });
  const lastVisible = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const list = document.querySelector(".page-navigation__list");
    const last = list.lastElementChild.getBoundingClientRect();
    const lr = list.getBoundingClientRect();
    return {
      scrollTop: list.scrollTop,
      lastInView: last.bottom <= lr.bottom + 1 && last.top >= lr.top - 1,
      lastLabel: list.lastElementChild.textContent.trim(),
    };
  });
  console.log("scrolled to bottom:", lastVisible);
  await page.screenshot({ path: `${OUT}/pages-bottom.png` });

  // wheel scrolling works too
  await page.evaluate(() => (document.querySelector(".page-navigation__list").scrollTop = 0));
  const box = await (await page.$(".page-navigation__list")).boundingBox();
  await page.mouse.move(box.x + box.width / 2, box.y + box.height / 2);
  await page.mouse.wheel({ deltaY: 400 });
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 300));
  console.log(
    "after wheel scrollTop:",
    await page.evaluate(() => document.querySelector(".page-navigation__list").scrollTop),
  );

  await clickByText("Enter clearing mode");
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 300));
  console.log("clearing mode:", await measure());
  await page.screenshot({ path: `${OUT}/pages-clearing.png` });

  await browser.close();
})().catch((e) => {
  console.error(e);
  process.exit(1);
});
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-19 04:26:32Z)**_

The page navigation menu now scrolls, so you can reach every page. I checked it in a real browser (headless Edge) with 10 pages:
- **Scrolling:** the mouse wheel scrolls the list, and scrolling to the bottom shows Page 10.
- **Buttons stay visible:** "Add page" and "Enter clearing mode" stay pinned below the list.
- **Clearing mode:** the same holds, with "Select all pages", "Clear" and "Exit clearing mode" pinned at the bottom.

**What was wrong:** the list already allowed scrolling, but the panels around it grew to fit every page instead of staying inside the sidebar. The sidebar then cut off the pages below the bottom of the window instead of scrolling them.

**The fix** is in `Pages.scss`, plus one class name added to the pages tab in `LayerUI.tsx`. The panels now keep to the sidebar's height, so the list takes the space left over and scrolls. Scrolling the list also no longer scrolls anything behind it, and the outline on the current page is no longer cut off at the edges. The sidebar's shared styles are untouched, so Library and Search behave as before.

The page tests (9) and typecheck still pass. There's no automated test for the scrolling itself, because the test environment doesn't calculate layout. Nothing is committed yet.

```text
**Code PR:** [feat(editor): implement group object functionality (#84)](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/pull/170) (open, awaiting review)

## What have you implemented so far, and what remains?

So far I have made a PR for my first issue (feat(editor): implement group object functionality (#84)). I still need to get that PR approved, and I need to begin working on and complete my second issue for the sprint. The issue that I complete made everyone who edits an element its co-owner, and makes the element follow the least restricted of its owners: it stays visible, and editable, as long as at least one co-owner is. It also changed collaborative behavior such as making the last change win (instead of the version that was changed the most ahead).

## What is one thing you learned about testing in your project?

One thing that I learned about testing in my project is that the tests are fairly hierarchical, so it is relatively easy to extend the existing ones when new features/functionalities are added. I also learned that there are certain cases that are not tested for, because of the way that certain things were implemented that should prevent those errors from occurring, but slightly tweaking certain things changes that behavior, and thus test cases have to be added. Also, certain functionality (such as Elements whose deletion was older than 24 hours could come back) wasn’t really tested for, so it seems there wasn’t strong direction on how certain things should behave, and their behavior was just accepted.

## What is one risk to finishing your work by Nov 19, and what will you do about it?

One risk is that I will rush the work and take cheap short cuts that will be detrimental to the health of the project in the long-run. For example, in this sprint, I built off of the existing functionality (using the existing way that different edits are merged and slightly changing it, instead of implementing an entirely new system). This may lead to me introducing more technical debt (ex. changes made at the same time on two devices whose clocks disagree, before they've exchanged anything, are still ordered by those clocks), when trying to implement less intensive fixes for issues that result from previous more core design decisions.
```

```text
  bindMode: { browser: true, export: false, server: false },

const _clearAppStateForStorage = <
  ExportType extends "export" | "browser" | "server",
>(
  appState: Partial<AppState>,
  exportType: ExportType,
) => {
  type ExportableKeys = {
    [K in keyof typeof APP_STATE_STORAGE_CONF]: typeof APP_STATE_STORAGE_CONF[K][ExportType] extends true
      ? K
      : never;
  }[keyof typeof APP_STATE_STORAGE_CONF];
  const stateForExport = {} as { [K in ExportableKeys]?: typeof appState[K] };
  for (const key of Object.keys(appState) as (keyof typeof appState)[]) {
    const propConfig = APP_STATE_STORAGE_CONF[key];
    if (propConfig?.[exportType]) {
      const nextValue = appState[key];

      // https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/31445
      (stateForExport as any)[key] = nextValue;
    }
  }
  return stateForExport;
};

export const clearAppStateForLocalStorage = (appState: Partial<AppState>) => {
  return _clearAppStateForStorage(appState, "browser");
};

export const cleanAppStateForExport = (appState: Partial<AppState>) => {
  return _clearAppStateForStorage(appState, "export");
};

export const clearAppStateForDatabase = (appState: Partial<AppState>) => {
  return _clearAppStateForStorage(appState, "server");
};
```

```bash
      expect(within(page1).queryByText("Current")).toBeNull();
      expect(page3.classList).toContain("page-navigation__item--current");
      expect(page1.classList).not.toContain("page-navigation__item--current");

      const checkbox2 = page2.querySelector(".page-navigation__checkbox")!;

      expect(checkbox2.textContent).toBe("");
      expect(page1.classList).toContain("page-navigation__item--selected");
      expect(page2.classList).not.toContain("page-navigation__item--selected");
    });

      fireEvent.click(getByRole("button", { name: "Clear" }));
      expect(document.querySelector(".confirm-dialog")).not.toBeNull();

      API.setAppState({ pageClearingSelection: null });
      await waitFor(() =>
        expect(document.querySelector(".confirm-dialog")).toBeNull(),

      expect(document.querySelector(".confirm-dialog")).toBeNull();
```

StrykerJS is set up with the Vitest runner. Both reports are committed on `feat/issue-159-page-clearing`, and nothing is pushed. The mutation score went from **69.67%** on the first run to **90.40%** on the re-run.

| Report | Killed | Survived | No coverage | Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/159-NotaThomas-before.json` | 147 | 62 | 2 | 69.67% |
| `docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/159-NotaThomas-after.json` | 179 | 17 | 2 | 90.40% |

I used `NotaThomas` as the username, taken from your sprint 3 check-in and AI-log folders. Tell me if it should be `ThomasReilly` instead, which is the name your sprint 2 diagrams use.

**Commits**
1. `75a4649d`: the page-clearing and scrolling feature.
2. `b85e28a0`: the Stryker setup and the before report.
3. `3b0de04e`: the new tests, small code cleanups and the after report.

I corrected the messages on commits 2 and 3 after making them, because I had misread a column and written "2 timeout" where it should be "2 no coverage".

**Setup**
- **Packages and script:** `@stryker-mutator/core` and `@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` 10.1.1. Run it with `yarn test:mutation`; a run takes about 6 minutes.
- **`stryker.config.mjs`:** mutates only the lines changed for #159, because the files themselves are large (`App.tsx` is over 12,000 lines). Reporters include `json`.
- **`vitest.stryker.config.mts`:** limits the run to the 5 test files that exercise that code. This keeps runs fast and stops unrelated tests from failing Stryker's first test pass, such as your untracked `pathPlaybackHold.test.tsx` (already failing) and the flaky Mermaid test.
- **`.gitignore`:** now ignores Stryker's temp folder and `reports/mutation/`.

**Between the runs**
- **New tests:** 12 tests that kill specific survivors, mostly UI states that weren't checked before. They cover:
  - the "Current" badge and check marks;
  - dialogs closing and showing the page count;
  - sidebar docking rules;
  - undo after clearing all pages;
  - keeping clearing mode out of saved and exported state.
- **Code cleanups:** I removed a few pieces of code that couldn't affect behavior, such as a check for an empty page list (there's always at least one page) and a CSS class nothing used.

**The 19 remaining mutants**
Each mutant either can't be reached or has no visible effect:
- defensive guards that only run if clearing state is changed outside the UI;
- passing the current page to `clearPages` twice, which still undoes in one step;
- the `"ui"` analytics label;
- class-name strings;
- `container?.focus()`, where the container is always present.

**Things to know**
- **Line ranges must be kept up to date.** If code in those files moves, the line ranges in `stryker.config.mjs` need updating.
- **Pre-commit hook reformats JSON.** The hook runs Prettier on `.json` files, and after one commit it reformatted the before report on disk. I checked the content was identical and restored the committed file. Expect this to happen again when committing reports.
- **Shared dialog flag between tests.** The Clear canvas dialog's open/closed flag is shared across tests, so the page tests now reset it before each one. Without that, a dialog left open by one test broke the next. This is the cross-editor dialog problem I flagged earlier.

```markdown
# Mutation testing: Issue #159 -- Implement Page Clearing

**PR(s):** Not opened yet (branch `feat/issue-159-page-clearing`) **Tool:** StrykerJS 10.1.1 with `@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` **Config:** [stryker.config.mjs](../../../stryker.config.mjs) + [vitest.stryker.config.mts](../../../vitest.stryker.config.mts) (my own setup, not reused from a teammate) **Command:** `yarn test:mutation`
**Reports:** [before](reports/159-NotaThomas-before.json) · [after](reports/159-NotaThomas-after.json)
**Mutation score:** before 69.67% → after 90.40%

Stryker mutates only the lines changed for #159 (listed as line ranges in `mutate`), and Vitest runs the five test files that exercise them: `pages.test.tsx`, `shortcuts.test.tsx`, `excalidraw.test.tsx`, `search.test.tsx` and `DefaultSidebar.test.tsx`.

| Run | Mutants | Killed | Survived | No coverage | Score |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before | 211 | 147 | 62 | 2 | 69.67% |
| After | 198 | 179 | 17 | 2 | 90.40% |

The after run has fewer mutants because I removed code whose mutants could not change any behavior: an always-true page-count check, an unused CSS modifier class, a conditional around resetting the confirmation, and a redundant `scope: "canvas"` argument.

## Surviving mutants

The table lists the 19 mutants still alive in the after report (17 survived, 2 no coverage). Line numbers refer to the after report. Paths are under `packages/excalidraw/`.

| Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `components/App.tsx:2777` | `getActivePageId` returns `undefined` | Equivalent | Its only caller is the "clear canvas and all pages" action, which filters out the current page. With `undefined`, the current page is also passed to `clearPages`, but the action clears that page in the same step anyway. The result is identical and still undoes in one step. |
| `components/App.tsx:2788` | `page.id !== this.activePageId` → `true` | Equivalent | This also empties the current page's saved copy in `this.pages`. That copy is stale while the page is open, and `saveActivePage` overwrites it from the scene before anything reads it. |
| `components/App.tsx:2825` | `!state.pageClearingSelection` → `false`; guard body → `{}` (no coverage) | Equivalent (unreachable) | `togglePageForClearing` is only called from the page checkboxes, which only render in clearing mode, so the selection is never `null` when it runs. |
| `components/App.tsx:2845` | `!selection?.length` → `false`; `?.` → `.`; guard body → `{}` (no coverage) | Equivalent (unreachable) | The Clear button is disabled when nothing is selected, and clearing an empty list of pages changes nothing. |
| `actions/actionCanvas.tsx:100` | `.filter(...)` removed; `id !== activePageId` → `true` | Equivalent | Same as `App.tsx:2777`: the current page is cleared twice in one step, with the same result and the same single undo step. |
| `components/ActiveConfirmDialog.tsx:17` | `!activeConfirmDialog` → `false`; body → `{}` | Equivalent | When no dialog is open (`null`), execution falls past the `"clearCanvas"` check to the final `return null`. |
| `components/ActiveConfirmDialog.tsx:21` | `activeConfirmDialog === "clearCanvas"` → `true` | Equivalent | The atom's type is `"clearCanvas" \| null`, and `null` has already returned at line 17. |
| `components/ActiveConfirmDialog.tsx:34` | action source `"ui"` → `""` | Equivalent (for the requirements) | The source string only goes to analytics (`trackAction`); nothing the user sees changes. Killing it would mean mocking analytics. |
| `components/ConfirmDialog.tsx:33` | default `className` `""` → `"Stryker was here!"` | Equivalent | It adds an extra CSS class that no stylesheet uses. |
| `components/ConfirmDialog.tsx:42` | `setIsLibraryMenuOpen(false)` → `true` | Test gap | After any confirm-dialog button is clicked, the Library tab's "…" dropdown would be left open. This is upstream behavior I moved into `runAndRefocus`; it isn't part of #159's requirements, and no test opens the Library after a dialog. |

But if the Pages panel remounts while clearing mode is on (closing and reopening the sidebar), the confirm dialog could render for one frame first. No test checks for the dialog right after reopening the sidebar. |

## New or strengthened test

Commit: [3b0de04e](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/commit/3b0de04e232c94dcffcedd2f9241b548a7322a72) · Test: `packages/excalidraw/tests/pages.test.tsx › pages › clearing mode details › indicates the current page and the selected pages only while clearing` · Kills (before-report lines): `components/Pages.tsx:179`, `:193`, `:195`, `:200`, `:204`, `:218`

This test covers three acceptance criteria. The clearing header, the checkboxes and the "Current" badge appear only in clearing mode. Only the page you are on is marked as current. A selected page shows a check mark and the selected style, and an unselected page does not.

The same commit adds 11 more tests that kill other former survivors, for example:

- `clearing mode details › clears only the current page when it is the only one selected` kills `App.tsx:2802` (cleared elements must not stay selected).
- `clearing mode details › refreshes the previews of cleared pages that aren't open` kills `App.tsx:2809` and `:2811` (the re-render after clearing pages that aren't open).
- `clearing mode details › drops a pending confirmation when clearing mode is closed` kills `Pages.tsx:165` and `:169`.
- `sidebar docking › doesn't dock the pages sidebar outside clearing mode` and `› doesn't dock other sidebar tabs during clearing mode` kill `DefaultSidebar.tsx:95` and `:96`.
- `clear canvas dialog › keeps everything when cancelled` and `› closes after clearing only the current page` kill `ActiveConfirmDialog.tsx:32`, `:39` and `:42`.
- `clearing mode details › never stores clearing mode with the drawing` kills the three `appState.ts:255` boolean mutants.

## Questions

1. **What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?**
   My first tests checked end results, such as which pages ended up empty, but rarely the states in between. Of the 62 survivors in the first run, most were in UI feedback the acceptance criteria require but no test asserted: the "Current" badge, the check marks, the clearing-mode header, the confirmation's page count, and dialogs closing after Confirm or Cancel. Others were design rules no test checked: when the sidebar docks, keeping clearing mode out of saved and exported state, clearing the selection after a clear, and refreshing previews of pages that aren't open. A few survivors showed the code itself could be simpler, so I removed four pieces of code that could not change behavior. Writing the new tests also exposed a test-isolation problem: the Clear canvas dialog's open/closed flag lives in a jotai store shared by every editor, so a dialog left open by one test leaked into the next. The page tests now reset it in `beforeEach`.

2. **Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements? Explain.**
   Yes, in two ways. First, while writing the test that kills the undo-related mutants for "clear canvas and all pages", my first expected value was that one undo would bring back every element on the current page. That assumption came from me, not from the requirements or from how Excalidraw works. The test failed because the helper had added that element outside undo history, and Excalidraw's undo can only restore changes it recorded. I changed the test to add an element in its own history step and expect only that element back. Second, several assertions I added test design decisions rather than the written acceptance criteria. Examples: cleared elements are deselected (`App.tsx:2802`), clearing mode is never saved (`appState.ts:255`), and the sidebar docks only for the pages tab in clearing mode (`DefaultSidebar.tsx:95–96`). The criteria only say the menu should open "to the side so that the user can still see the page", so docking is my reading of that criterion. These are reasonable expectations, but they come from the implementation, and the team should confirm them.

3. **If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and what did you verify or correct?**
   I used Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) for all three. It installed StrykerJS and the Vitest runner, wrote `stryker.config.mjs` and `vitest.stryker.config.mts`, ran both mutation runs, classified the survivors in the table above, made the four code simplifications, and wrote the 12 new tests. Corrections made along the way:
   - The first configuration left `excalidraw-app/` out of Stryker's sandbox copy. The dry run then failed because the test helpers import from it, so that exclusion was removed.
   - The undo test's expected value was wrong and was corrected (see question 2).
   - After the code simplifications moved lines, the `mutate` line ranges were recomputed from the diff so the re-run covers the same changed code.
   - Two commit messages misread Stryker's summary table, reporting "2 timeout" where the table meant "2 no coverage". The messages were corrected, and the counts above come straight from the JSON reports.
   - The JSON reports were reformatted for readability, and their parsed content was checked against Stryker's original output.

   Each test change was verified by running the five Stryker test files, plus typecheck and lint, before the re-run.
```

Closes #84

## Why

Issue #84 (child of #14). Hiding and locking collaborators (#81) was based only on who *created* an element. Once someone edited another person's element, the element still followed only its creator's visibility and lock settings, so a collaborator you had chosen to keep visible could have their work hidden or locked away. This issue makes everyone who edits an element its co-owner, and makes the element follow the least restricted of its owners: it stays visible, and editable, as long as at least one co-owner is.

Working through how co-ownership behaves in a live room exposed several sync problems, which this PR also fixes:
- Conflicting edits were decided by "the copy changed the most times wins", so a long drag beat a later delete.
- Concurrent co-owner stamps could overwrite each other.
- Changes from other users made during your drag, resize or text edit were silently dropped.
- Elements whose deletion was older than 24 hours could come back.

## What changed

- **Co-ownership data:** `customData.creatorId` still records the creator. New fields:
  - `customData.editorIds`: the current co-owners.
  - `customData.editorSeqs`: a counter per client, bumped each time that client is added or removed. It makes the co-owner list mergeable: only each client changes its own entry, so the higher counter is the newer state, and a removed co-owner keeps their counter as a marker so an older copy can't add them back.
- **Becoming a co-owner (`packages/element/src/ownership.ts`, `packages/element/src/store.ts`, `App.tsx`):**
  - A new `Store.onBeforeDurableCaptureEmitter` fires just before a local change is saved to undo history.
  - At that point, `getElementsToCoOwn` finds elements the user edited directly (selected, or text being edited) but doesn't own, and stamps the user as a co-owner as part of the **same undo step**.
  - Side effects don't count: rerouted arrows, frame children, z-order, `boundElements`.
  - Editing a label co-owns its shape.
- **Least-restricted-owner rule:**
  - `isElementByHiddenCreator`: an element is hidden only if **every** owner is hidden.
  - `isElementInteractive`: it can be interacted with if **any** owner is interactive.

  Rendering, hit testing, selection, the eraser, export, search and arrow binding all go through these two functions, so all of them follow the new rule. "Hide all" and the per-row drawing counts include co-owners.
- **Undo/redo (`packages/excalidraw/history.ts`):**
  - Undoing every edit a user made to an element removes them as a co-owner; redo adds them back.
  - Undo/redo normally restores the whole `customData` object. A merge step now keeps other clients' co-ownership as it was, so only the current user's entry follows history.
- **Latest change wins (`packages/common/src/clock.ts`, `packages/excalidraw/data/reconcile.ts`):**
  - A hybrid logical clock stamps `updated`: it follows the wall clock, never goes backwards, has a logical counter for changes within the same millisecond, and jumps forward when it sees a newer remote timestamp (capped at 60 s ahead of the local clock).
  - It's stored in the same `updated` number as `ms + counter/1024`, so the format doesn't change.
  - Reconcile now keeps the copy with the later timestamp. It falls back to the old version/nonce rules for same-millisecond changes and for old data without timestamps.
  - Co-owner lists are merged from both copies instead of being taken from the winner.
- **Incoming changes during edits in progress (new module `packages/excalidraw/data/inProgressEdit.ts`):**
  - Covers resizing or rotating one element, text editing, drawing a new element, dragging, and multi-element transforms.
  - Each edit owns some properties: geometry for all of them, plus the text for a text edit and `frameId` for a drag. A newer remote change to any *other* property is merged into the local element. For example, a recolour made during your drag survives.
  - A newer remote delete:
    - **text edit, single-element resize, drawing, multi-element transform:** cancels the edit;
    - **drag:** removes just that element, and the rest keep moving.

    Either way, the editor re-issues the delete with a later timestamp so it sticks, and shows a notice.
  - Stale copies made before the edit started are ignored.
  - To support cancelling, the text editor now returns `{ submit, cancel }`, and `App` keeps a reference to the active pointer gesture.
- **Expired deletions (new module `excalidraw-app/collab/expiredDeletions.ts`):** deleted elements stop syncing 24 hours after deletion.
  - **The rule:** a live element the room's stored scene doesn't have, which this client synced before, and which hasn't changed in over 24 hours, was deleted.
  - **When saving to Firebase:** such elements are left out of the save and deleted locally.
  - **When receiving an update:** old live elements this client doesn't have are ignored. Age is measured with the sender's clock, via a new optional `sentAt` field on scene updates, so a client whose clock is far behind can still add elements.
- **Strings:** `collaboratorEdit.deletedWhileEditing` added to `en.json`.

## Tech Debt

### Introduced

- **One edit per page:** the in-progress-edit registry (`inProgressEdit.ts`) and the element clock (`elementClock`) are module-level singletons. Two Excalidraw editors on the same page would share them.
- **Co-owner removal markers are never cleaned up.** `editorSeqs` keeps an entry for every client that ever co-owned an element.
- **Fractional timestamps:** `updated` can now have a fractional part. External tools that assume whole milliseconds will see fractions. The encoding is exact until about the year 2248.
- **Deploy all clients together:** clients running the old rule and the new rule can settle on different copies of a conflicting element. Reloading the page fixes it.
- **Edits not covered by the in-progress handling:** line/arrow point editing, cropping and arrow-key nudges still use plain "latest change wins". During those continuous edits, remote changes are mostly lost.
- **Cancelling an edit loses work:**
  - Cancelling a multi-element transform leaves the other elements where they were mid-gesture. Nothing is rolled back, and they're only recorded in undo with the next change.
  - Cancelling a text edit loses the text typed so far.
- **The delete notice doesn't say who deleted the element**, and the new string is in `en.json` only.
- **Expiry false positive:** a live element whose Firebase saves failed for over 24 hours can be treated as an expired deletion. Some peers may not see it until the next successful save brings it back.
- **Clock skew isn't solved:** changes made at the same time on two devices whose clocks disagree, before they've exchanged anything, are still ordered by those clocks. The 60 s cap limits how far a wrong clock can push others.

### Encountered

- **Arrow-key moves aren't saved as their own undo step;** they're folded into the next one. This also delays co-ownership from an arrow-key move until that next step.
- **The text editor and pointer gestures had no way to cancel.** Both were added for this PR.
- **`getUpdatedTimestamp()` returns `1` in tests.** Every existing test therefore runs on the version fallback, and the new time-ordering tests set timestamps explicitly.
- **Test failures not caused by this PR:**
  - `pathPlaybackHold.test.tsx` (an untracked file in the working tree, not part of this PR) was already failing before this work.
  - `pathMotionConfig.test.tsx` ("a 300px path at 0.5x speed plays for 2000ms") and `history.test.tsx` ("should create new history entry on scene import via drag&drop") failed once each under full-suite load and passed when run alone.
- **Remote updates during a gesture update the store snapshot mid-gesture,** so that gesture's undo step can be partial. This was already the case for drags and is unchanged by this PR.

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Joint ownership tracking | `coOwnership.test.tsx`: "editing a collaborator's element adds me as a co-owner, keeping the creator", "selecting without editing doesn't", "editing my own element doesn't add me as a co-owner", "a co-owned element counts for each owner in the menu"; `coOwnership.test.ts` (element): "a selected, edited element someone else created gets me as co-owner", "an element changed as a side effect (not selected) doesn't", "elements I already own don't", "new, deleted, unstamped or merely re-indexed elements don't", "editing a label co-owns its shape", "does nothing outside of a room (no self id)", "moving or restyling is an edit", "bookkeeping, z-order and binding references are not", "lists the creator first, then co-owners, without duplicates", "bound text follows its container's owners", "keeps concurrent co-owners from both copies", "is commutative: both orders give the same co-owners"; `reconcileClock.test.ts`: "concurrent co-owner stamps both survive, whichever copy wins" | unit, integration | AC, issue discussion |
| B: Shared visibility evaluation | `coOwnership.test.tsx` › "visibility of a co-owned element (rendering, AC-B)": "(control) without co-owners, hiding the creator hides the element", "after I edit it, hiding its creator keeps it on my canvas and in exports", "it's hidden once every one of its co-owners is hidden", "a peer's co-owned element stays visible while any co-owner is visible", "shows again as soon as one co-owner is shown again"; also "once I co-own it, locking its creator doesn't lock it for me", "without co-owning, locking its creator deselects it (unchanged)"; `coOwnership.test.ts` › "least restricted owner rule" (7 tests, including "Bob locked, Carol not → interactive for Alice" and "Bob hidden, Carol visible → visible and interactive") | unit, integration | AC, issue discussion (the Alice/Bob/Carol example) |
| C: Dynamic ownership updates | `coOwnership.test.tsx`: "editing it again doesn't add me twice", "undoing my only edit removes me as a co-owner, redo adds me back", "I stay a co-owner until ALL my edits to the element are undone", "undo keeps co-owners other clients added in the meantime", "undoing an unrelated edit doesn't touch my co-ownership"; `coOwnership.test.ts` › "reconcileEditorIdsAfterHistory" (5 tests), "getCoOwnedCustomData adds me with a new counter and keeps other custom data", "a newer removal beats an older copy that still lists the co-owner", "a newer re-add beats an older removal"; `reconcileClock.test.ts`: "an undone co-ownership stays removed against a stale copy", "merging into the local winner keeps the same element object" | unit, integration | AC, issue discussion (undo rule) |
| Beyond the ACs: latest change wins | `reconcileClock.test.ts` › "HybridClock" (10 tests), "reconcileElements — the latest change wins" (6 tests, each checking that both clients end up with the same element) | unit | issue discussion; upstream behavior (the version/nonce fallbacks) |
| Beyond the ACs: incoming changes during edits | `inProgressEdit.test.tsx`: "getMergeableRemoteChanges" (2), "while resizing" (7), "while editing text" (2), "while dragging" (4), "while transforming several elements" (2) | integration | issue discussion; numbers such as `width` 130 and `x` 20 worked out by hand from the pointer moves |
| Beyond the ACs: expired deletions | `expiredDeletions.test.ts`: "isPastDeletionExpiry" (2), "getExpiredResurrections" (4), "getLocalElementsWithExpiredDeletion" (5) | unit | issue discussion; existing `DELETED_ELEMENT_TIMEOUT` (24 h) |

**Not tested automatically, and why:**
- No criterion was checked only by hand, and no manual checks were done.
- Real collaboration between two browsers (relay server and Firebase) isn't covered. The tests apply remote updates through `reconcileElements` or `updateScene` directly, so Collab, Portal and the socket/Firebase code paths aren't exercised.
- Groups as "drawing clusters" (AC-A) have no dedicated test. Co-ownership is per element, so editing a group stamps each edited member, but no test checks that.
- The expiry rules are unit-tested, but their wiring into `Collab.tsx` and `firebase.ts` is not. No test simulates a tab offline for more than 24 hours.

```text
Implement Page Clearing
enhancement
# Issue Description

## Summary
Allow users to remove elements from individual pages, multiple selected pages, or all pages without deleting the pages themselves.

## User Story
**As a** user, **I want** to be able to clear pages **so that** I can get rid of mistakes that I make and remove elements that I no longer want.

## User Scenario
Developer adds the wrong diagram to one of their pages. The developer selected 'clear', which puts them in clearing mode, then selects 'clear current page', which deletes all elements on the current page. The developer then selects 'cancel' which returns them to normal mode. 

---

# Issue Classification

## Scope

**Generic:** Medium
**Specific:** Lesser medium (5 points)
**Reason:** Clearing mode where user can select the individual pages they want to clear or mass select all pages to clear them all. Changing currently existing clear canvas functionality to work within the paradigm that the pages are sub-canvases of the main canvas. Changes to UI and underlying functionality.

---

# Expectations

## Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] **Clearing mode:** There should be a button that says 'enter clearing mode' around/in the navigation menu. When it is pressed, it should open a menu to the side so that the user can still see the page they are on. The menu should have an augmented navigation menu that displays all the pages and indicates in some way the page the user is currently on. There should be a 'clear' option and an option to exit clearing mode. 
* [ ] **Clear selection:** The user should be able to select the pages they want to clear from the augmented menu. The user should also be able to choose to select all pages. The pages they have selected should indicate that they have been selected. 
* [ ] **Clearing confirmation:** When the user selects the 'clear' option while in clearing mode, the user should be prompted to confirm their choice. If the user confirms it, then pages that were selected from the augmented menu should be cleared. 
* [ ] **Closing clearing mode:** The clearing options should only be visible when in clearing mode. Clearing mode should remain open until the user selects the exit option, which closes clearing mode. 
* [ ] **Clearing mode across page groups:** If there are two drawings that have pages, entering clearing mode in one should not enter clearing mode in the other, and exiting clearing mode in one should not exit clearing mode in the other. 
* [ ] **Clear canvas option:** There is already a clear canvas option that exists in Excalidraw. We are considering the pages to be 'sub-canvases', so the pre-existing clear canvas option should be changed to give the user the option to clear the canvas and all sub-canvases, or just the canvas. 

## Open Question

* How should the pages selected to be cleared be indicated to the user? For example, should there be a checked box next to the selected pages?
* Should the user should still be able to navigate to different pages while in clearing mode?
* Should there be anything additional to indicated to the user that they are in clearing mode? For example, a banner telling the user that they are currently in clearing mode?

---

# Extra

## Out of Scope

* Deleting pages
* Changing anything about the properties of pages themselves that are unrelated to the elements on the page (the page order, page names, etc.)
* Undo/redo functionality
* Creating pages
* Transferring elements from one page to another (ex. copying and pasting elements between pages)

## Head Issue

Issue (#149): Multiple pages in one drawing

## Dependencies
```
